newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Violence threatens fair poll in Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Violence threatens fair poll in Sri Lanka.

text.p: Growing violence in the runup to Sri Lanka's local government poll later this month could affect the fairness of the election, a spokesman for an independent monitoring group said on Sunday.

Paikiasothy Saravanamuttu, of the Centre for Monitoring Election Violence, said they were appealing to all political parties to do whatever necessary to end the rising incidence of violence in the campaign for the March 21 poll.

"Right now the violence is not threatening the actual holding of the election," Saravanamuttu said. "But there are just far too many incidents of violence taking place and they are obviously going to have an adverse impact on a free and fair election and the democratic process."
The centre said that almost 500 incidents of election-related violence, mostly threats against candidates and their supporters, had been reported up to Friday.
The poll will be the ruling People's Alliance (PA) coalition's first popularity test since winning power in 1994.

"In this country we've had elections in the context of violence but it is important we move to a situation where violence is not part and parcel of the election process," said Saravanamuttu, who is also a member of the Coalition Against Political Violence.
He was referring to general elections held in 1989 during a leftwing youth insurgency in which human rights groups said some 60,000 people died or disappeared.
Police have launched an island-wide crackdown on unlicensed guns to curb political violence before the poll, already marred by the killing of a PA lawmaker earlier this month.
Police said 17 suspects were in custody for the killing of MP Nalanda Ellawala on the eve of nominations for the poll.
Among them were opposition United National Party (UNP) politician Susantha Punchinilame and Mahinda Ratnatilleke, a former mayor.
Former prime minister and UNP leader Ranil Wickremesinghe last week accused the government and police of turning a blind eye to large-scale attacks against party candidates.
More than 18,000 candidates from 12 political parties, including the PA, the UNP and 132 independent groups, will take part in the polls for 238 local government bodies.
